name: Cleaning a messy wetlab data resource
description: the procedure for bringing a messy repository of wetlab data into canonical form — the defect catalogue, what is mechanical, what the owner must decide, and why the output is a new folder rather than edits in place
phrases: fix a repository of oligos and plasmids
bring a project folder into canonical form
what is wrong with this data
notes: A PROMPT, NOT AN ALGORITHM. JCA 2026-09-14: "This clearly is a messy process requiring lots of 'how do you want to handle this one' questions, so it is prompt-like, not algorithm-like. But we will be doing it many times." The detectors are code; every resolution is a question for the owner of the data. Output is a new folder beside the original, which the owner then deletes — never edits in place, because a diff of 200 scattered edits is unreadable and rewriting every file states that every file is correct. Each entry in the catalogue was found in a real repository; two were found by a detector's first run against real data, which is the argument for returning what you could not read instead of dropping it.
